subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned session authentication gate, or should this remain a plugin/API-extension pattern built on `before_tool_call`?
rationale: The request crosses config, secret handling, session state, reset semantics, and fail-closed tool execution, so automation should not pick the security boundary or default behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a core SecretRef-backed gate
options.body: Add a core primitive only after specifying secret storage, trusted verification, reset behavior, transcript redaction, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Treat the current hook surface as sufficient and document or extend the plugin API so deployments can opt into session gates outside core.

options.title: Defer the PIN gate
options.body: Leave existing allowlists, sandboxing, approvals, and external-content wrapping as the supported mitigation until a stronger step-up-auth design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Design a core SecretRef-backed gate
recommendation.body: Add a core primitive only after specifying secret storage, trusted verification, reset behavior, transcript redaction, and compatibility expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across the affected session/tool/config paths and is already in the timeline context for this security/product decision.
